newsitem.title: USA: Jan American Eagle gold coin sales well up on 1996.
newsitem.headline: Jan American Eagle gold coin sales well up on 1996.

text.p: Sales of American Eagle gold and silver bullion coin sales in January were well up from the same month last year, industry consultant CPM Group said.
Demand for American Eagle gold coins totaled 51,250 ounces in January, up nearly fivefold from January 1996.
Spot gold prices were at a five-year high of $417.00 an ounce in early 1996, but fell to a three-year low of $336.00 early this year, analysts pointed out.
Similarly, American Eagle silver coins sales amounted to 435,000 ounces last month, 14 times more than in January 1996.

However, sales of American Eagle gold coins in January were down 27.8 percent from December 1996 for seasonal reasons, while sales of American Eagle silver coins were only about one third of December's level.

"It should be noted that the U.S. Mint offered investors the opportunity to order newly dated coins on the last business day of the year for the second year running," CPM Group said. "Investors and dealers took advantage of the offer and December sales spiked up to 1.34 million ounces for the American silver Eagle and 71,000 ounces for the gold American Eagle coins."
Meanwhile, sales of platinum bullion coins are soaring, according to dealers, with a rise in demand seen in late December and early January as bargain hunters entered the market.
Premiums for platinum coins generally firmed, while gold and silver premiums fluctuated in January.
